kata.name: Mediator near-floor control - a one-hub, one-interaction star where the frozen per-arrow suite catches both injected faults
kata.series_report: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md mediator row (disposed; discovery-only candidate); fixtures/katas/mediator/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-r5k.5
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: with a single declared mediator every dispatch-coherence cell is forced by range, so the coherence law has no fault class at the floor; the bypass and the documented-route swap are both caught by the frozen per-arrow suite, and the probe buys zero unique detections (killed)

expected.detail: interaction i_ab has dispatched_by null; the per-arrow suite asserts the cell resolves, the kernel emits an executed dangling finding on arrow dispatched_by, row i_ab: the same element

i_ab documents alice->bob but carries bob->alice; the documented route lives outside the model, so no kernel law mentions it. The pre-registered baseline route assertion catches it; the probe is silent

commands: python3 prototype/mediator_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: 5 entries, 3 unique elements; baseline sha256 pinned
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/mediator/near-floor.ct.json --json  # exit 0, findings []
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/mediator/near-floor-fault-bypass.ct.json --json  # exit 4, 1 dangling
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/mediator/near-floor-fault-route.ct.json --json  # exit 0, findings []

comparison.conventional_baseline: prototype/mediator_baseline.py --assert: a frozen per-arrow suite (hub/party/dispatch range assertions plus the documented-route table) over every row; catches both injected faults (2/2), zero unique detections for the probe.

baseline.artifact: prototype/mediator_baseline.py sha256:863b8c04a045b7571242b172540e0ba172aece8df9071ba37dd0263460b456d3 (frozen per-arrow suite: hub/party/dispatch range assertions plus the documented-route table; always executed before the probe arm)

expressibility_gap.invariant: the documented (speaker, listener) route of an interaction is enforced
expressibility_gap.why: the route table is external spec data; the model carries the same values as cells, and the route-swap variant is rename-isomorphic to the clean control (identical model hash), so no model hash or schema law can see it. Only the pre-registered baseline assertion does

discrepancies: The route-swap fault is invisible to the model: near-floor.ct.json and near-floor-fault-route.ct.json share model hash sha256:8103ca8c... because swapping speaker/listener is a renaming under the schema's symmetry. The control therefore measures the baseline's documented-route assertion, not a modeling win or loss.
procedure: 1. The law was named before any fixture was written (README: dispatch coherence `dispatched_by = participant ; hub`; exclusivity and absence named as the discovery-only and inexpressible halves). The fault set and its expectations were committed in fixtures/katas/mediator/ (README.md, faults.json) before the recorded run; nothing here is edited after the run.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/mediator_baseline.py, sha256 above) was executed first: per-arrow assertions over every row (colleague hub declared; interaction parties declared and distinct; dispatch declared; documented route matched). It never composes two arrows and never asserts a specific mediator row.
3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real CLI: `catherine check --json`, plus `catherine underconstraint --max-path-length 2 --json` where the discovery question belongs to the entry.

4. Witnesses were mapped to presentation elements (<object>:<name>); unique_detections = executed probe elements minus baseline-identified elements. Hypothesized underconstraint findings are questions, recorded verbatim and never counted as detections.
5. Verdict follows the recorded rule: empty unique = killed; non-empty unique with an executed baseline arm = survived.
